citations.claim: post-bounce velocity larger magnitude than pre-bounce

counterfactual.change: changed body e from 1.0 to 0.8, keeping all other fields same; inelastic loss compensates spurious gain, so energy_bound no longer violated

explanation: Elastic bounce with e=1 and semi-implicit Euler substeps injects energy. Body falls under gravity, hits floor between steps 55-56, and rebounds with higher speed (12.36 -> 14.19 m/s) causing total mechanical energy to jump from ~83.86 J to 108.99 J, exceeding initial energy 84.05 J + tolerance (allow 97.45 J). Positional correction plus restitution impulse appears to over-add velocity, violating energy conservation for e=1. Reducing restitution to <1 makes dissipation mask the gain.
vision_note: From steps 53 to 55 the blue body falls toward the floor, and in step 56 it is at the bottom boundary contacting the floor where the bounce should occur. No upward motion is visible yet in the strip, but the visual failure point is exactly the floor collision that the numeric trace flags as gaining energy.
